description: Excel's data cleanup on a Svelte 5 spreadsheet grid: a CRM export that landed in column A, semicolon-separated, with the same people in it twice. Data > Text to Columns opens a wizard that has guessed the delimiter and previews the split; Data > Remove Duplicates lets you tick the columns that decide identity, compares case-insensitively as Excel does, and reports how many duplicates went and how many unique rows remain. Each operation is one undo step. Enterprise, in @svgrid/enterprise.

faq.question: How does Text to Columns pick the delimiter?
faq.answer: The wizard scores tab, semicolon, comma, pipe and space over the selected rows: a delimiter that appears in most rows, the same number of times in each, wins; a comma in one row out of fifty is prose. The preview shows the split before anything is written.

faq.question: Which columns decide a duplicate?
faq.answer: The ones ticked in the Remove Duplicates dialog. Two rows are the same when those columns match, compared case-insensitively, and the first occurrence stays.

faq.question: Can a cleanup be undone?
faq.answer: Yes. Both operations write through the command context in one batch, so Ctrl+Z restores the column or the removed rows in one press.
